title: Replacing Weight Updates with Verbal RL

beats.text: Most AI agents are goldfish. Resetting their entire brain every time they fail a simple task.
beats.visual_focus: A digital goldfish bowl where a neural network icon resets its weights to zero.

visual_blueprint.title: THE MEMORY PARADOX
visual_blueprint.sub: Why traditional fine-tuning fails at rapid adaptation

motif_params.title: THE MEMORY PARADOX
motif_params.sub: Why traditional fine-tuning fails at rapid adaptation

beats.text: The villain? Expensive gradient descent. It forces us to burn massive compute just to nudge a few parameters for one minor mistake.
beats.visual_focus: A massive GPU cluster glowing red, struggling to process a single tiny weight update.

visual_blueprint.title: THE COMPUTE WALL
visual_blueprint.sub: Weight updates are slow and brittle

motif_params.title: THE COMPUTE WALL
motif_params.sub: Weight updates are slow and brittle

beats.text: Reflexion flips the script. Instead of changing weights. The agent writes a verbal critique of its own past failures.
beats.visual_focus: A text buffer filling with 'Self-Reflection' logs, acting as an external memory bank.

beats.text: It stores these reflections in an episodic buffer. The model then prompts itself with this wisdom to guide the next attempt.
beats.visual_focus: A loop diagram showing: Task -> Feedback -> Reflection -> Memory -> Improved Prompt.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: Dude, this was actually so clean. The goldfish opening immediately hooked me because it's punchy, funny, and instantly relatable if you've ever watched an LLM repeat the exact same dumb syntax error four times in a row. You explained Reflexion without dumbing it down into baby talk or drowning me in backprop math. Swapping weight updates for self-reflective prompting clicked right away.
